diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/7 is approaching saturation during peak periods: current traffic is 912 Mbps with a recorded peak of 948 Mbps, consistent with the customer's evening-only slowdown. The customer’s optical link, ONU, authentication, VLAN, router, and OLT are healthy.
evidence: The complaint is time-correlated with evening usage rather than a continuous loss of service.
The ONU is online and responding; RX power is normal at approximately -21.27 dBm and TX power is normal at approximately 2.37 dBm.
Seven days of optical telemetry are stable: RX variation is within the healthy noise range, TX power is stable, TX bias is healthy and flat, and distance remains constant.
The normal session count is only 2 in the last 24 hours with an average duration of 711 minutes, so there is no session flapping.
RADIUS state and CRM line ID are consistent, the VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1017, and the router heartbeat is healthy.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, all tested PONs are healthy, and OLT resource levels do not indicate an OLT-wide failure.
EPON0/7 is carrying 912 Mbps currently against a 948 Mbps peak, indicating peak-period shared-port saturation and explaining the evening throughput degradation.

remediation.action: Review EPON0/7 utilization and per-ONU traffic during the evening peak. Rebalance customers across PON ports, upgrade or split the port/splitter if capacity remains insufficient, and verify service performance after the change.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/7 carries 47 customers and its evening load is reaching 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average, close to the port's shared capacity ceiling. Throughput degrades for everyone on the port during peak hours. No optical or authentication fault exists.
expected_reasoning: The complaint is time-of-day specific, which points at load rather than at a physical fault
RX is flat at -21.2 dBm inside the noise floor, and TX, bias, voltage and distance are all stable
The live probe shows every ONU on the port online with normal optical readings
RADIUS is clean and sessions are long and stable, so authentication is not involved
PON port traffic is at 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average
Daily traffic for this customer is roughly three times the network mean and rising, not falling
Every fault-driven degradation reduces traffic; congestion raises it, so the direction is the discriminator
The customer's own throughput series drops sharply during the same evening hours each day
The port carries 47 customers, at the top of the observed occupancy distribution
This is capacity exhaustion on a shared port, not a fault on any one line

expected_escalation.review_reason: EPON0/7 needs a capacity review; 47 customers on one port with evening load near ceiling

distractors: Multi-customer slowness resembles a splitter or feeder degradation
Elevated OLT CPU and temperature could be read as device stress causing the slowness
Reduced throughput in the speed series looks like a link problem
